title: Map a controller with nonstandard button labels
summary: Map an unfamiliar controller by physical position and observed events, document every conversion to PS2 symbols, and test one press, release, diagonals, and shoulders.
heroAlt: OnePad legacy mapping window illustrating manual assignment for a controller whose printed labels do not match PS2 symbols

blocks.text: Build a position map before trusting any legend
Translate physical positions and observed Android events into PS2 functions when the shell uses Nintendo letters, arcade numbers, mobile symbols, or undocumented labels.
Guessing from printed letters can exchange Cross and Circle or Square and Triangle while still producing a superficially complete map.
Photograph and number the physical controls

items: Controller kept in one Android mode throughout the procedure.
Blank or backed-up Port 1 profile ready for manual mapping.
Paper or digital diagram showing face-button positions and shoulders.

blocks.text: Translate one physical location at a time

items: 1. Number the face buttons south, east, west, and north on a controller photo.
2. Press each numbered button in the Android event view and record its code.
3. Bind those positions to Cross, Circle, Square, and Triangle by PS2 location.
4. Map D-pad, shoulders, triggers, stick clicks, Start, and Select separately.
5. Reject automatic entries that refer to controls absent from the shell.
6. Test one press and one release for every mapped function.
7. Check simultaneous stick-plus-button input in a playable scene.
8. Save the profile with the controller model, mode, and layout convention.

blocks.text: A position-to-function worksheet remains valid across unfamiliar legends, whereas copying letters assumes conventions that the controller may not use.
Every physical position activates one documented PS2 function and the finished diagram matches menus plus gameplay.

items: The controller photo and saved profile agree control by control.
PS2 prompts correspond to physical positions rather than misleading letters.
No unknown event code remains attached to two functions.
South and east actions are swapped: remap by PS2 position, not letter.
One button emits a keyboard key too: disable the duplicate device mode or binding.
Automatic mapping creates nonexistent controls: clear it and retain the manual map.
A mode switch changes all codes: return to the documented stable mode.

blocks.text: Import the prior profile and archive the rejected position worksheet.
Shell legends describe a convention, not Android identity
Third-party pads can reuse familiar artwork while exposing a different event order, so only observed codes and physical positions are reliable.
